o1.biggest_strength: It brings back the pause as the main save, splits the reasons by plan and reminder status, and makes the money maths clear.
o1.biggest_mistake: The upside range is not fully derived and leans on untested switch/reminder assumptions.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Show the range calculation explicitly, add a small holdout test plan, and confirm the billing pause can be rebuilt before sprint start.

o2.biggest_strength: It gives a very complete one-screen flow with exact copy, segment counts and build/test notes.
o2.biggest_mistake: It keeps a 50% discount for switching-app leavers and adds unsupported offers like a smaller daily goal, which weakens the margin discipline.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Remove or clearly test the unsupported 50%-off and smaller-goal offers, and make every retained group tie back to evidence and owner economics.

reason: Output 1 is the one I'd hand to the team: it restores the pause, segments by plan and reminder status, does the maths transparently and keeps discounts away from people who will return anyway. Output 2 is useful, but its extra 50%-off and smaller-goal offers feel less grounded.
